title: Assessing crae and support needs of families with children and adolescents diagnosed with cancer predisposition syndromes
summary:
Cancer predisposition syndromes (CPS) are identified in approximately 10% of pediatric cancer patients, with an increasing number of affected families each year. Despite the known psychosocial challenges faced by these families, including uncertainty in communication, genetic risk implications, and lifelong surveillance, there is limited data on the specific support needs of families in Germany. Understanding these needs is critical to improve family-centered care and psychosocial support systems. 

KiTDS-Care systematically assesses the current situation of care for families with a child with CPS, including psychosocial stressors, support needs, and derives recommendations  for (psychosocial) care.

Online-based survey (quantitative) of parents with a child with CPS regarding mental well-being, quality of life, and care situation (sample size: n = 90)
